Summary_EN: A power supply equipment failure on Line 11 has led to speed restrictions between Malu and Wuwei Road and longer service headways. Delays of approximately 15 min are expected.

External track intrusion on Line 11 has led to speed restrictions between Malu and Wuwei Road and longer service headways. The disruption is expected to last approximately 30 min. The emergency shuttle bus plan between Jiading Xincheng and Wuwei Road has been activated.

External construction activities have damaged Line 11 trackside equipment and a train, forcing the train to stop between stations. Emergency repairs and passenger evacuation are underway. No injuries have been reported at the site.

Line 11 equipment and a train have been damaged, and repairs will require considerable time. Passengers traveling from Wuwei Road toward Jiading are advised to use surface transport. An apology is issued for the inconvenience.

A tower crane involved in external construction has intruded into the line, damaging Line 11 infrastructure and a train. Conditions at the site are complex, and repairs are expected to take considerable time. Passengers traveling from Wuwei Road toward Jiading should use surface transport rather than Line 11. Passengers traveling from Wuwei Road toward the central city can continue to use Line 11.

Emergency repairs continue on the damaged Line 11 section, and service cannot be restored in the short term. Operations are adjusted to three short-turn routes: North Jiading–Malu, Huaqiao–Malu, and Wuwei Road–Disney Resort. A shuttle bus operates outside stations between Jiading Xincheng and Wuwei Road. Passengers traveling from Wuwei Road toward Jiading are advised to use surface transport.

Summary_EN: Shentong Metro Group reports that, following intensive emergency repairs, the damaged Line 11 section is expected to reopen at approximately 21:00 that evening.

Summary_EN: Service on the damaged section first resumes in the direction from Chenxiang Highway toward Disney Resort. Source: Xinhua News Agency, citing Shanghai Metro.

Summary_EN: Trains toward Jiading resume operation, largely restoring bidirectional service on the damaged section. Source: Xinhua News Agency.

The Shanghai Meteorological Center issues a blue typhoon warning, forecasting gusts of force 8 or above from the afternoon of September 15 to the afternoon of September 16. It advises precautions against adverse effects on work at height, travel, and protected agriculture.

The typhoon warning is upgraded from blue to yellow, with gusts of force 10 or above expected from around midnight to the following afternoon. A blue high-water-level warning is issued for the Huangpu River, with the peak water level at the mouth of Suzhou Creek forecast to exceed 4.55 m at approximately 12:00 on September 16. A citywide Level III flood and typhoon emergency response is activated.

Before landfall, typhoon and flood preparedness plans are deployed across operations, construction, and asset management. Managers, staff, and emergency personnel are assigned to 24 h duty, and hazard inspections and precautionary preparations are carried out.

Plans account for passenger flows leaving and returning to Shanghai during the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday. Trains are prepared for early depot departure and track inspection, and service patterns, speed-restricted sections, and emergency coordination plans are refined. Measures are adjusted according to warning levels, ridership trends, and control measures at neighboring stations to prevent passenger accumulation and crowding.

Station responsibilities for typhoon preparedness are specified in greater detail. Emergency drills cover passenger evacuation, resource deployment, and equipment repairs to assess the practicality of the plans.

Warning monitoring and passenger flow guidance are strengthened. Additional staff are assigned to escalators, entrances and exits, and transfer passages, with more frequent public-address announcements and on-site guidance.

The metro enters typhoon response mode. Train suspension and passenger evacuation will be organized if hazardous conditions arise. Depending on the typhoon's development, services on at-grade and elevated sections may be shortened or suspended.

The typhoon warning is upgraded from yellow to orange, with gusts of force 12 or above forecast in most areas from the early hours of the following morning through the afternoon and a very high risk of damage. A citywide Level II flood and typhoon emergency response is activated. Residents are advised to avoid nonessential travel, and all city parks close immediately. The blue Huangpu River high-water-level warning and red wave warning remain in force.

Intelligent operation and maintenance systems and online monitoring platforms are used to monitor infrastructure, equipment, and the track environment. Emergency materials and personnel are deployed in advance, repair teams remain on 24 h standby, and emergency resources are positioned in priority areas.

From 21:30 on September 15, Maglev service ends early and speed restrictions apply to at-grade and elevated sections of Lines 2, 5, 11, and 16 and the Pujiang Line. From the start of service on September 16, Lines 3, 5, 16, and 17, the Pujiang Line, and the Maglev Line are fully suspended, together with at-grade and elevated sections of Lines 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11. Restoration times will be announced separately.

Drainage equipment at the Maglev maintenance base is inspected and sump water levels are lowered in advance. Patrols and flood-response preparations are strengthened. Excavations, tower cranes, and temporary electrical installations at construction sites are checked for hazards, with emergency supplies and duty arrangements put in place.

The early termination of Maglev service at 21:30 on September 15 and speed restrictions on relevant at-grade and elevated sections are announced again. Full suspension of six lines and suspension of at-grade and elevated sections on nine lines on September 16 are confirmed. Passengers are advised to follow official channels for restoration information.

The early end of Maglev service, speed restrictions on relevant sections, and full or partial suspensions the following day are reiterated. Restoration times for suspended sections will depend on typhoon conditions and will be announced through official channels.

A yellow rainstorm warning is issued, forecasting short-duration intense rainfall exceeding 50 mm/h from the early hours of the following morning through the afternoon. Precautions against urban waterlogging and drainage measures in low-lying areas are advised. The orange typhoon, red wave, and blue Huangpu River high-water-level warnings remain in force.

The red wave warning remains in force, with wave heights of 5.0–7.0 m expected offshore of the Yangtze River estuary during the early morning and morning. Waters within the estuary and around Yangshan Port reach orange warning levels, while the northern waters of Hangzhou Bay reach the yellow level. The orange typhoon, yellow rainstorm, and blue Huangpu River high-water-level warnings remain in force.

Full suspension of Lines 3, 5, 16, and 17, the Pujiang Line, and the Maglev Line is confirmed, together with suspension of at-grade and elevated sections on nine lines. The notice specifically identifies the Shanghai South Railway Station–Xinzhuang and Shanghai Railway Station–Fujin Road sections of Line 1 and the Guanglan Road–Pudong International Airport section of Line 2 as suspended. Passengers are advised to use other modes.

The extent of full-line and at-grade/elevated section suspensions is reiterated. Passengers are advised not to travel to stations on suspended sections and to plan routes before departure. Restoration times will be announced according to typhoon conditions.

The notice reports 155 stations suspended and 351 operating normally. Lines 12, 13, 14, 15, and 18 operate normally; Lines 3, 5, 16, and 17 and the Pujiang Line are suspended; and Lines 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11 operate on shortened routes. Restoration times will be announced separately.
Line 2 is adjusted to operate between East Xujing and Longyang Road, with the Longyang Road–Pudong International Airport section suspended. Passengers are advised to adjust their routes.

The rainstorm warning is upgraded from yellow to orange, with accumulated rainfall of 100 mm or more expected in most areas over the next 6 h. Precautions against urban waterlogging, farmland inundation, and traffic congestion are advised. The red wave, orange typhoon, and blue Huangpu River high-water-level warnings remain in force.

The lists of normally operating, fully suspended, and shortened-service lines are issued again. Line 2 operates between East Xujing and Longyang Road, with Longyang Road–Pudong International Airport suspended. The Luheng Road–Shendu Highway section of Line 8 and the Songjiang Xincheng–Zhongchun Road section of Line 9 are also suspended.
The operator will gradually restore suspended sections as typhoon impacts permit and safety can be ensured. Passengers are advised to follow official information.
Line 1 is adjusted to operate between Shanghai Railway Station and Xujiahui. The Xujiahui–Xinzhuang and Fujin Road–Shanghai Railway Station sections are suspended.

Gradual restoration is scheduled from 14:00 for the at-grade and elevated sections of Line 8 and the full Maglev and Pujiang lines. Other listed suspended sections remain closed. Speed restrictions and longer headways may apply during restoration.

Gradual restoration is scheduled from 14:30 for the at-grade and elevated sections of Lines 2, 7, and 9. Relevant sections of Lines 1, 4, 6, 10, and 11 and the full lengths of Lines 3, 5, 16, and 17 remain suspended. Speed restrictions and longer headways may apply during restoration.

Gradual restoration of the full length of Line 17 is scheduled from 15:00. Relevant sections of Lines 1, 4, 6, 10, and 11 and the full lengths of Lines 3, 5, and 16 remain suspended. Speed restrictions and longer headways may apply during restoration.

Gradual restoration of the full length of Line 16 is scheduled from 15:15. Relevant sections of Lines 1, 4, 6, 10, and 11 and the full lengths of Lines 3 and 5 remain suspended. Speed restrictions and longer headways may apply during restoration.

The orange typhoon warning is downgraded to blue at 15:20, with southerly winds of force 7–8 still expected over the next 6 h. The orange rainstorm warning is lifted at 15:35. The red wave warning is downgraded to blue, while the blue Huangpu River high-water-level warning remains in force.

Gradual restoration of the at-grade and elevated sections of Line 10 is scheduled from 15:45. Relevant sections of Lines 1, 4, 6, and 11 and the full lengths of Lines 3 and 5 remain suspended. Speed restrictions and longer headways may apply during restoration.

Gradual restoration is scheduled from 16:20 for the at-grade and elevated sections of Lines 1, 4, and 11 and the full length of Line 3, excluding the Huaqiao–Zhaofeng Road section of Line 11. That section, relevant sections of Line 6, and the full length of Line 5 remain suspended.

Gradual restoration is scheduled from 16:40 for suspended sections of Line 6, excluding Jufeng Road–Gangcheng Road, and for Huaqiao–Zhaofeng Road on Line 11. Jufeng Road–Gangcheng Road on Line 6 and the full length of Line 5 remain suspended.
Gradual restoration of the full length of Line 5 is scheduled from 17:00, with possible speed restrictions and longer headways. Jufeng Road–Gangcheng Road on Line 6 remains suspended.

The typhoon moves away from Shanghai and winds weaken substantially. The blue typhoon warning is lifted at 18:00. The blue Huangpu River high-water-level warning was lifted at 16:30. Wave heights in coastal waters decrease, and the blue wave warning is lifted at 18:00.

Gradual restoration of Jufeng Road–Gangcheng Road on Line 6 is scheduled from 18:20, completing the restoration of services on all lines across the network. Speed restrictions and longer headways may still apply on some sections during restoration.

The notice confirms that suspended at-grade and elevated sections have been progressively restored and that all lines across the Shanghai Metro network have resumed normal operation. Passengers are advised that they can use rail transit with confidence.
